title: How many degrees are the three angles at H?
description: Three angles with the same vertex H are measured one by one with a protractor. The centre goes on the vertex, one arm goes on the zero line, and the number is read where the other arm crosses the scale. Each reading is then checked against a right angle.
teaching_notes: One idea: place the centre on the vertex and one arm on zero, then read the scale that starts at that zero. Watch for students who read the scale that starts at the wrong end.

source: Figure it Out (after Angle Bisector), Q1
video_script.why: The child measures three angles with the protractor by the three checks of the solved example, and checks each reading against a right angle.
video_script.substitution: The three angles at the vertex H of the book's question.
video_script.anchor: the three angles of the book, each with its vertex at H and a small arc
video_script.payoff_line: The three angles measure forty seven, twenty three and one hundred and eight degrees

final_answer.spoken: forty seven degrees, twenty three degrees and one hundred and eight degrees

maths_rules: first angle at H reads 47 degrees
second angle at H reads 23 degrees
third angle at H reads 108 degrees
a right angle is 90 degrees; 47 < 90, 23 < 90 and 108 > 90
the count starts at 0 on the arm that lies on the zero line
video_script.design: The three angles stay on the board. One protractor is placed on each in turn by the same steps, and the readings are held back until the answer line.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book, with three angles drawn.
<bookmark mark='three'/>Each angle has the same vertex, the point aitch, and a small arc.
We have to find how many degrees each angle has.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Before we measure, which angle looks the widest, and which looks the narrowest?

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

narration: <bookmark mark='way'/>We measure the same way as the example in your book.
<bookmark mark='centre'/>The centre of the protractor goes on the vertex.
<bookmark mark='zero'/>One arm goes along the zero line, and we read the scale that starts at that zero.

beats.on_screen: Given: three angles with the same vertex H, each marked with a small arc

marks.given: the three angles are listed under the word Given

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, three angles that have the same vertex aitch, each with a small arc.

beats.on_screen: To find: the degree measure of each angle
narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the degree measure of each angle.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: put the centre of the protractor on the vertex H

marks.centre: the protractor slides until its centre point meets H
marks.why: a tick appears beside the centre point

beats.moves_through: the protractor slides onto the vertex
narration: <bookmark mark='centre'/>Step one, put the centre of the protractor exactly on the vertex aitch.
<bookmark mark='why'/>An angle is measured at its vertex, so the centre must sit there.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: turn the protractor until one arm lies along the 0 line

marks.turn: the protractor turns until one arm meets the zero line
marks.scale: the scale that starts at that zero is circled

beats.moves_through: the protractor turns about the vertex
narration: <bookmark mark='turn'/>Step two, turn the protractor until one arm lies along the zero line.
<bookmark mark='scale'/>We read the scale that starts at that zero.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: read the number on that scale where the other arm crosses it

marks.read: the other arm is followed out to the scale and the mark it crosses lights up

narration: <bookmark mark='read'/>Step three, follow the other arm out to the scale, and read the number where it crosses.
That number is the measure of the angle in degrees.

beats.on_screen: Step 4: repeat steps 1 to 3 for the second angle and then the third angle

marks.again: the protractor moves to the second angle and then to the third angle

beats.moves_through: the protractor moves from one angle to the next
narration: <bookmark mark='again'/>Step four, do the same three steps for the second angle, and then for the third angle.

beats.on_screen: Step 5: check each reading with a right angle, 90°; narrower than a right angle reads less than 90, wider reads more

marks.right: a right angle is drawn beside each angle
marks.check: a tick or a cross appears under each reading

narration: <bookmark mark='right'/>Step five, check each reading with a right angle, which is ninety degrees.
<bookmark mark='check'/>An angle narrower than a right angle must read less than ninety. A wider angle must read more.

beats.on_screen: Answer: first angle 47°, second angle 23°, third angle 108°

marks.ans: the three readings are boxed, one under each angle

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The three angles measure forty seven, twenty three and one hundred and eight degrees.
They match the order we read, first, second and third.
